name: Clark S. Willes, Attorney at Law
tagline: Second Chances Won in the Courtroom
brandNarrative:
Clark S. Willes is a Corvallis criminal defense attorney who fights hardest when the stakes are highest. Clients facing Measure 11 felony charges — mandatory minimum offenses that carry the weight of years behind bars — have walked out of court with their freedom intact and their families whole. As one client put it after beating his felony charge: 'I got to stay with my family and be surrounded by love.' That kind of outcome doesn't happen by accident. It happens because Clark knows the law cold and works it relentlessly.

His reputation in DUI defense runs deep across Linn County and its neighbors. Former clients describe him as the single best DUI attorney in multiple counties — someone who not only delivers results but works with clients on finances when they need it most. He's the attorney people whisper about when they're sitting in a jail cell, the one other inmates recommend by name. That word-of-mouth credibility, earned case by case, is the foundation of everything this practice stands for.

The honest picture here is a small, focused solo practice with a fiercely loyal core of clients and a handful of frustrated ones. The attorney who does 'nothing only when there is nothing he can do' operates on courthouse logic, not customer service scripts — which wins cases but doesn't always win phone tag. For clients who understand that a quiet attorney can be a working attorney, Clark Willes delivers outcomes that transform lives.
ownerStory:
Clark S. Willes built his practice the way most Willamette Valley criminal defense attorneys do — one hard case at a time. Operating from a suite on NW 4th Street in downtown Corvallis, just blocks from the Benton County Courthouse, Clark has spent years in the trenches of Oregon's criminal justice system. He knows Measure 11. He knows DUI law. And he knows the difference between a case that looks hopeless and one that still has a thread worth pulling. The clients who trust that instinct tend to walk free.

His practice is deliberately lean — weekday hours, a modest suite, no marketing machine. What he offers instead is access to a legal mind that former clients describe in near-reverent terms: 'honestly a legal expert,' 'a wonderful attorney,' 'the best.' For a solo practitioner in a mid-sized Oregon city, that kind of earned reputation is the whole business model. Clark is not for everyone. He is for the person staring down a felony charge who needs someone who genuinely knows how to win.

team.name: Clark S. Willes
team.bio: Described by clients as 'honestly a legal expert' and the best DUI attorney in multiple counties, Clark has successfully defended clients against Measure 11 felonies and serious criminal charges throughout the Willamette Valley. He is proactive when there are moves to make and candid when there aren't — a courtroom-first approach that wins cases.

faq.question: Can Clark Willes actually beat serious felony charges like Measure 11?
faq.answer: Yes — and it's one of the things clients mention most. One client facing a Measure 11 felony charge wrote that he 'honestly didn't think he had a chance' before Clark took the case. He beat the charge and went home to his family. Measure 11 cases carry mandatory prison sentences with no early release, which makes experienced, aggressive defense critical.

faq.question: Is Clark Willes really the best DUI attorney in the area?
faq.answer: Multiple clients say so without reservation. One former client described him as 'the best DUI attorney in probably multiple counties — for sure Linn County and the neighbors.' He's known for working deals in court and for being willing to work with clients on payment when finances are tight.

faq.question: Will Clark return my calls and keep me updated?
faq.answer: This is the most honest tension in the practice. Some clients report excellent outcomes with minimal friction. Others have found communication frustrating, particularly around return calls and scheduling visits. Clark is a solo practitioner with a courthouse-focused style — if you need frequent updates, discuss that expectation clearly at the outset.

faq.question: Does Clark work with clients on payment and legal fees?
faq.answer: Yes. Multiple clients specifically mention that he is willing to work with clients on finances. As one DUI client put it: 'he will work with you with finances. Of course you have to pay him — he is worth it.'

faq.question: What hours is the office available?
faq.answer: The office is open Monday through Thursday from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, and Friday from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM. The office is closed on weekends. For urgent criminal matters outside office hours, call (541) 758-0071 and leave a detailed message.

faq.question: What types of criminal cases does Clark handle?
faq.answer: Clark's practice centers on serious criminal defense — particularly Measure 11 felonies and DUI cases. Client reviews also mention he works 'really good deals for other crimes,' suggesting a broad criminal defense practice. Contact the office at (541) 758-0071 to discuss your specific situation.

brandColors.note: Deep navy conveys courtroom authority and trust — essential for criminal defense where clients are at their most vulnerable. Gold accent signals competence and outcome-focused confidence without corporate coldness. This pairing reads as experienced, serious, and on your side — not institutional.
